note.name: Monero
note.thesis: The balance of evidence tilts lower, but not strongly enough for a directional view: fee demand has not grown against a $10.49B valuation, and crowded longs sit on a falling seven-day trend. Fixed supply caps the downside.
note.what: Monero is a proof-of-work payments chain where every transaction hides sender, amount and receiver by default, using ring signatures, RingCT and stealth addresses. It mines with RandomX on ordinary CPUs, one block about every two minutes. Its users are people who need money to move without a public trail: remittance corridors, merchants settling through swap services, and privacy-first savers.

points.text: Fee demand runs at $1.54M annualised against a $10.49B FDV — 6821.4× fees, versus a 240.2× peer median.
Revenue is $0 lifetime: all fees are wages for miners, and there is no treasury, burn or buyback.
Miner issuance is near $88M a year against roughly $1.5M of fee demand, about 50:1; miners are the only structural sellers.
7-day funding of +0.0831%/8h is above XMR's usual +0.0043%–+0.0619% range, while open interest fell 13.2% and price lost 12.6% in 7 days.
All 18.83M XMR already circulates and supply grows about 0.21% a quarter, with no insiders holding coins to sell.

note.supplyHeadline: No unlocks; miners get new coins
note.supplyText: Nothing is scheduled to unlock over the next 90 days: all supply already circulates and new coins go only to miners as block rewards. Tail emission has been fixed at 0.6 XMR per two-minute block since June 2022, and daily issuance ran about 293–446 XMR over 4–11 Nov 2026.
note.valuationText: Fees are the right yardstick for a Layer 1 whose holders have no claim on protocol income; revenue is zero, so a revenue multiple cannot be drawn at all. Across the fee peer set the range runs from 41.0× (Polygon) to 1016.5× (Ethereum), and XMR sits above the top of it.
note.usageText: Daily fee demand is roughly $3.8k; the 30-day total of $126,362 barely exceeds the 7-day pace of $29,715, so nothing is accelerating. There are no staking rewards, airdrops, points, treasury or buyback to manufacture activity — all of it is organic, and all of it is small.

risks.title: Monetary framing wins
risks.text: If buyers value XMR against bitcoin and gold rather than network fees, the cash-flow gap loses much of its force.

risks.title: Fee demand re-rates
risks.text: Seven-day annualised fees above the 30-day pace for two straight weeks would undercut the flat-demand case.

risks.title: Only miners sell
risks.text: No unlocks, no insiders and slow issuance leave miners as the only sellers, so a demand shift can move price sharply.

risks.title: FCMP++ gets dated
risks.text: A dated FCMP++ mainnet announcement is the identified upside trigger and would lift the upgrade premium.

watchlist.item: FCMP++ mainnet launch has no announced date
Kraken removal and Dubai privacy-token ban shrank distribution

note.positioningText: Hyperliquid funding is +0.7023%/8h now against a 7-day average of +0.0831%/8h. Open interest across exchanges is $52M, down 13.2% over seven days, and the long/short account ratio is 1.04, with 51% of accounts long.
note.conclusion: Monero's evidence is split rather than conflicting: cash-flow tests make it the most expensive name in its peer set, fee demand has not grown, and the seven-day trend is down with longs crowded. Fixed supply, no unlocks and no insiders limit the sell side. The balance tilts lower, but not strongly enough for a directional view.
note.invalidation: 7-day annualised fees above the 30-day pace for two straight weeks.
note.gaps: No FCMP++ mainnet date exists outside the project's own research page. Zcash and Dash FDV and revenue are missing, so the privacy peer comparison is incomplete. KYC-free exchange volume totals are not available from DefiLlama or Nansen.
